glossary.means: A small program Cloudflare runs close to the reader, for each request it is asked to answer.
Cloudflare's SQL database. Only the Worker can reach it.
Cloudflare's file storage, for whole files like a day's card data.
A single, named place in Cloudflare that keeps state and runs code for it; here, one per game.
Cloudflare's sign-in gate. It lets through only invited people and tells the Worker who they are.
A signed note that proves who someone is for a short time.
The browser's own database, on the reader's device.
A script the browser keeps beside a site so it can open and work offline.
Where a service worker keeps copies of files.
Browser storage that lasts only as long as the tab.
A network that serves the same files from many places, close to each reader.
One large download of a whole data set, instead of one request per record.
A small file naming the newest good copy of each data set.
A number added to a file's address so a browser fetches the new copy after a change.
A connection that stays open so updates arrive as they happen, without asking again.
The CrankMagic Engine: our own implementation of the game's rules.
The ordered list of every action in a game; replaying it gives the same game.
A saved copy of a game's state so it can resume after a restart.
The one interface the engine saves through, so the same engine runs in a test or a game room.
The engine's own opponent. It sees only its seat and costs nothing to run.
What a player may not see: another player's hand, the order of a library.
The list of places a page may load from or talk to. The browser enforces it.
The browser's rule for when a page may read another site's answer.
The standard way one service asks another, such as Google, who a person is.
Signing in with a second proof, such as a passkey.
The list of people allowed to use something.
A direct connection Cloudflare sets up between a Worker and a database or bucket, with no address to attack.
Show the saved copy now and quietly fetch a fresh one.
A saved copy of something as it was at one moment.
The version every device should end up with.
Wizards' complete rules of the game, numbered.
A card's official, current rules text.
Cloudflare's command-line tool for deploying Workers.
GitHub's machines that run jobs on a push or a schedule.
Rob's tool that maps a codebase into a graph. This page is drawn from it.

req:M1-archidekt.text: Import from an Archidekt link through a Worker route, with a size limit and nothing stored.

req:M1-delete-account.text: Delete account: a Worker route removes the person's snapshots, head and user row; removing them from Access stays Rob's runbook step.

req:M1-design.text: The web app follows the r3 design system: its tokens, Satoshi type and the brass accent, in dark and light.

req:M1-landing.text: A landing page at / for a signed-out visitor with no library in the browser; anyone else goes straight to Decks.

req:M1-notify.text: For a signed-in person, 'Tell me when it's ready' on Play is a switch stored with the account; no mailing list.

req:M1-precons.text: Start from a precon, from a list refreshed with the card data from MTGJSON.

req:M1-settings.text: A Settings page: Account, Appearance, Prices (US dollars), Data, and About with every data set's date and the version.

req:M10-finish.text: The Coach's logic through the AI door, the Lab's data-driven strategy, and the accounts' later features if Rob still wants them.

req:M2-adjudication.text: A rules adjudication log citing the CR, the card's rulings, the release notes and the Commander page, and a scheduled Comprehensive Rules check.

req:M2-ages.text: Settings › About shows every data set's date, and anything past its lifetime is labeled stale.

req:M2-csp.text: The browser reaches only api.scryfall.com and loads images only from Scryfall's CDNs; every other source goes through the Worker or the scheduled job.

req:M2-images.text: Card images always come from Scryfall's CDN, through the browser's and the worker's caches, and are never stored by us.

req:M2-live-first.text: Outside data is read live first, then from the reader's cache (IndexedDB: 7 days for records, 24 hours for prices), then from a refreshed store.

req:M2-offline.text: Offline still works: the worker keeps the last good copy of every stored set and the reader's cache keeps what they opened.

req:M2-pin.text: A game pins the oracle snapshot and card-definition version it started with, so a replay is identical.

req:M2-schedule.text: A scheduled GitHub Actions run of tools/refresh.mjs publishes dated keys and current.json to R2 and keeps 7 runs; a run that fails its proof publishes nothing.

req:M2-serve.text: The Worker serves /data/* from R2, and the app reads current.json in place of ?v= pins.

req:M2-stores.text: Stores only where live cannot do the job: the name index, the engine's oracle snapshot, one dated price snapshot, EDHREC ranks and co-play, precons, and our derived graph and strategies.

req:M2-terms.text: Honor each source's terms: Scryfall's User-Agent, rate and bulk files; EDHREC read gently on a schedule; Wizards' texts cited and not redistributed.

req:M3-backups.text: D1 Time Travel's window confirmed, and a nightly export of D1 to R2.

req:M3-invite.text: Accounts are invite-only through the Access 'Invited' policy; the free plan caps it at 50 people.

req:M3-monitoring.text: Workers observability logs, alerts on 5xx and on sync conflicts, and a weekly check.

req:M3-rate-limits.text: Rate limits on /api/*, per identity and per IP.

req:M4-engine.text: CME plays Rob's seven decks deterministically with hidden information held, writing its journal and checkpoints through a storage adapter.

req:M4-house-pilot.text: The house pilot, the engine's own opponent, sees only its seat and costs nothing per game.

req:M4-legality.text: Deck legality is checked at prepare against a dated banned list, refusing by name.

req:M5-definitions.text: Card definitions are served to the room from R2, not bundled.

req:M5-front-door.text: The Worker creates, joins and leaves tables and hands a seat to an Access identity; identity stays out of the engine.

req:M5-hidden.text: Hidden information holds in network payloads, logs and reconnect snapshots.

req:M5-lobby.text: The lobby per r3's 2b design: invites by email, link and QR, table rules, and auto-launch that waits for every human seat.

req:M5-reconnect.text: Reconnect sends a fresh permitted view; a game never concedes silently and AI takes over only by agreement.

req:M5-results.text: A finished game files its record under the deck and syncs with the account; a guest's deck never overwrites the host's library.

req:M5-room.text: One Durable Object per match runs CME, holds the authoritative state and hides hands.

req:M5-transport.text: A WebSocket on the Durable Object carries ordered view updates and receipts, with no polling.

req:M6-door.text: The AI door: its own Access application (Google with MFA, never the emailed code), an AI allowlist in D1, the key as a Worker secret, spend caps, and a log of every call.

req:M6-privacy.text: The privacy page says what goes to the AI before any AI feature is switched on.

req:M7-compiler.text: Every card is compiled and reconciled into card definitions shipped as data; a card that cannot be is refused, naming what it lacks.

req:M8-playtest.text: A playtest table on staging for Grok Bot's four agents, whose games export seed, journal and per-seat projections.

req:S1-one-address.text: One address serves the app, crankmagic.com, and the only public contact is admin@crankmagic.com.

req:S1-release.text: The web app is released from one commit of main through release/pages and deployed with wrangler after the acceptance walk passes, staging first.

req:S2-access.text: Every /api/* request passes Cloudflare Access and is verified again by the Worker: signature, audience, issuer, expiry and a named person.

req:S2-sync.text: A signed-in person's library saves itself to the cloud and follows them to any device; a conflict is put to the person and the other version is held 30 days.
